title: OpenAI Agents approval-aware evidence
nextDecision: Decide whether to run a bounded local spike after the next radar review.

capabilityDelta.baseline: Recorded AIM and Git observations without provider approval lifecycle metadata
capabilityDelta.candidate: Preserve handoffs, guardrails, approvals, interruptions and resumed attempts as evidence
capabilityDelta.alternative: Discard provider lifecycle metadata and analyze only completed tool calls
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Identity and approval-state retention across pause/resume fixtures
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: A tool call requiring approval, rejection and later resumption

hypothesis.statement: Approval-aware mapping can reduce unknown lifecycle states without creating false independent-candidate classifications
hypothesis.invalidationResult: The mapping loses attempt ownership or produces a stronger classification than the input evidence supports

evidencePlan: Build synthetic pause, approve, reject and resume records
Compare retained identity, effects, versions and uncertainty with the provider-neutral baseline
Record unknown rate and false-safe classifications
risks: Provider-specific state may be unstable
Approval metadata may contain sensitive arguments
Tracing does not prove execution authorization
limits: No adapter correctness or market superiority is established

title: MCP asynchronous task and state analysis
nextDecision: Decide whether a pinned MCP task version and synthetic fixture are available for a spike.

capabilityDelta.baseline: Tool-call evidence without a portable lifecycle for deferred results
capabilityDelta.candidate: Preserve task IDs, status, TTL, protocol version and explicit state handles
capabilityDelta.alternative: Flatten each deferred call into an unversioned completed operation
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Task/state identity and version retention across polling fixtures
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: A task transitions from working to failed or completed while the caller resumes

hypothesis.statement: Explicit task and state metadata can improve provenance coverage for asynchronous operations while preserving unknown on unsupported semantics
hypothesis.invalidationResult: Flattening or protocol-version ambiguity causes a stronger result than the source permits

evidencePlan: Create synthetic tasks/get, task result and state-handle records
Check identity, version, dependency and effect preservation
Measure unknown classifications for unsupported task extensions
risks: MCP proposals and SDK support may differ
State handles can expose sensitive context
Protocol conformance is not semantic independence
limits: No MCP runtime or SDK is installed
The track does not adopt a protocol version

title: A2A conformance-backed task evidence
nextDecision: Reassess after a versioned A2A conformance artifact is selected.

capabilityDelta.baseline: No cross-agent protocol adapter in the current analyzer
capabilityDelta.candidate: Retain task timelines, artifacts, streaming events and conformance metadata in AIM evidence
capabilityDelta.alternative: Treat remote agent messages as opaque unstructured text
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Preserved task/artifact identity and event ordering in a synthetic A2A trace
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: Two agents exchange a task, artifact update and terminal event

hypothesis.statement: A conformance-backed A2A projection can make cross-agent ordering evidence inspectable without inventing independence
hypothesis.invalidationResult: The selected A2A version or TCK cannot preserve event identity and provenance

evidencePlan: Select and pin one protocol version
Use a synthetic fixture and TCK-compatible event inventory
Compare ordering and unknown behavior with a provider-neutral baseline
risks: A2A extensions and TCK are evolving
Remote artifacts may carry credentials or personal data
Interoperability does not establish semantic commutation
decisionRationale: Keep as a post-M2 candidate until a protocol version and conformance artifact are selected.
limits: No A2A adapter or conformance execution is included

title: OpenTelemetry evidence transport
nextDecision: Reassess after the monthly radar review confirms convention and privacy stability.
sourceNote: Weekly radar candidate captured on 2026-09-23; not a committed historical radar snapshot.

capabilityDelta.baseline: No generic trace transport for external agent and tool observations
capabilityDelta.candidate: Ingest optional spans and events while preserving source boundaries and redaction
capabilityDelta.alternative: Require provider-specific trace parsers or capture raw prompt content
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Identity/effect retention and redaction rate on synthetic traces
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: An agent span contains model, tool and token metadata with sensitive content disabled

hypothesis.statement: A vendor-neutral trace bridge can broaden evidence ingestion without making experimental telemetry conventions normative
hypothesis.invalidationResult: The bridge requires sensitive content, loses provenance or raises assurance without stable conventions

evidencePlan: Use synthetic OTel-like records only
Test metadata-only and sensitive-content-disabled modes
Measure retained fields, redactions and unknown rate
risks: GenAI conventions remain experimental
Trace payloads can contain secrets or personal data
Telemetry is observation, not execution authorization
decisionRationale: Observe convention stability and privacy requirements before a spike.
limits: No OpenTelemetry dependency or collector is introduced

title: CoAgent/MTPO research comparator
nextDecision: Decide whether an artifact-level reproduction is feasible at M2.

capabilityDelta.baseline: Agent Braid bounded Git and AIM analysis with no runtime transaction protocol
capabilityDelta.candidate: Compare advisory serialization, repair and undo assumptions against Agent Braid's evidence model
capabilityDelta.alternative: Treat the paper's reported metrics as direct proof of a better algorithm
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Reproduced semantics, workload coverage, unknown behavior and cost under matched fixtures
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: Shared-state agent operations with declared footprints and a conflicting write

hypothesis.statement: A bounded semantic comparison can identify complementary or contradictory assumptions without adopting the paper's runtime protocol
hypothesis.invalidationResult: The artifact or semantics cannot be reproduced sufficiently to support a fair comparison

evidencePlan: Obtain and inspect the authors' artifact if available
Map assumptions to AIM and operational semantics
Report positive, negative or inconclusive reproduction separately
risks: The source is an unreproduced preprint
Runtime assumptions differ from Agent Braid's read-only boundary
Throughput comparisons may double-count incompatible workloads
decisionRationale: Keep as an M2 scientific comparator; do not incorporate MTPO into the scheduler.
limits: No reproduction or algorithm adoption is included

title: Claude Code dynamic workflows integration (M4.6, SPEC-052/053)
nextDecision: Founder review of SPEC-052/053 and the feature-local adr-proposal, then preregistration and execution of gate G0; the kill criterion applies if G0 closes g0-fail (criterion C1b, C2, C3 attribution coverage of changed files below 0.60, or C4 unmet on the first 10 eligible runs with probe data); g0-inconclusive keeps the transcript requirements blocked and is not support.

capabilityDelta.baseline: A Claude workflow with worktree agents whose results the user integrates manually, optionally with a git merge-tree per-file conflict check
capabilityDelta.candidate: A read-only gate packaged in the native plugin that returns commit-level evidence, a merge-tree baseline, and for at most four operations a replay certificate, plus transcript-derived read/write hazards only if G0 passes; a one-way adapter into AIM, never granting execution authority
capabilityDelta.alternative: clash-style pairwise merge-tree detection and advisory path leases (mcp_agent_mail), which operate at file or text level
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Preregistered at G0 (docs/experiments/CLAUDE_WORKFLOW_INTEGRATION_PROPOSAL.md) on designed runs: whether transcript read/write overlap flags an attributable semantic failure that merge-tree, naive path overlap and commit-level Braid analysis all miss (C1b), its precision against prevalence and naive precision (C2), the attribution coverage of changed files by transcript write calls (C3) and its response on negative controls (C4), reported with hits and misses, replay-ineligible rate and analysis cost; operator effort and order independence are not measured by G0; no speed metric (parallel runtime speedup is NO-GO in SPEC-021, SPEC-022 and SPEC-038)
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: Bounded set of real or recorded Claude workflow runs with two to four worktree agents, run on the founder's existing Claude subscription with EUR 0 additional spend

hypothesis.statement: Read/write overlap derived from recorded Claude subagent transcripts surfaces integration failures that git merge-tree baselines, naive path overlap and commit-level Braid analysis do not. At commit level the Braid primary flag equals naive path overlap plus unknown labelling, so no extra commit-level detection is claimed, and order independence is not tested by G0. This is a differentiation hypothesis, untested.
hypothesis.invalidationResult: G0 closes g0-fail: no attributable transcript-only failure (C1b), precision at or below the floors (C2), attribution coverage of changed files below 0.60 (C3), or a probe that responds to negative controls (C4); the track then closes as watch, rejected or research-only and SPEC-053 is not pursued. A g0-pass means feasibility not refuted, not adoption; g0-inconclusive is not support.

evidencePlan: Preregister gate G0 (corpus, baseline, metrics, kill criterion) before any run
Host-verify the unconfirmed behaviors: plugin MCP tools and plugin agents inside workflow agents, and nested plugin workflow calls
Run the read-only gate on the bounded corpus and compare against the merge-tree baseline
Report positive, negative and inconclusive outcomes separately; keep obtainedEvidence empty until recorded
risks: Host behaviors for plugin MCP tools, plugin agents and nested plugin workflows are unconfirmed
Transcript-derived effects may be mostly unknown, limiting hazard evidence
The platform vendor may add native conflict detection, removing the gap
Adopting this track amends ADR 0024 and touches the SPEC-023 trace adapter boundary, requiring a separate ADR and founder decision
Demand for this evidence is not established
limits: No evidence obtained; human review pending
Not adoption, host compatibility or superiority; a stage record only
Moving beyond this stage requires the Spec Kit features, an ADR and a founder decision per the adoption pathline

title: Claude Code orchestrator coordination: advisory pre-flight, continuous checks and opt-in guard (M4.6, SPEC-057/058/059)
nextDecision: Founder review of SPEC-057, SPEC-058 and the SPEC-059 sketch, then preregistration of experiment G1 for SPEC-057; repeat the dated prior-art pass before any wording implying uniqueness and before SPEC-058 release. Kill criterion: G1 shows no incremental caught-conflicts or reduced late conflicts over baseline A0 (prompt partitioning per the host's published guidance, the worktree or isolation flag where the surface offers it, and the SPEC-052 end-of-run gate with git merge-tree as comparator), or host verification shows the guard does not fire inside subagents. G1 adds a native-controls-only arm (founder-written permissions.deny and sandbox rules, with no Agent Braid output) beside baseline A0 and the other arms; until that arm has a recorded result, no claim is made against permissions.deny or sandbox settings alone, and a GG pass would not show that the compiler or guard adds anything over them.

capabilityDelta.baseline: A Claude orchestrator (workflow script, linked or background sessions, agent teams or /batch) that partitions work by instruction, relies on native worktree isolation and native permissions, and meets conflicts at integration time, optionally with file-level tools such as path leases or merge-tree prediction
capabilityDelta.candidate: An advisory core (SPEC-057) that maps declared ownership to pre-flight verdicts, checks declared-versus-observed envelopes at quiescent checkpoints and reports recovery inventories, with pull-based notices (Mailbox plus Whisper by default; monitor, channel and own-session socket transports are opt-in and deferred to SPEC-059); the differentiation hypothesis rests on the combination of an Article 13 compatibility class, pairwise classification that includes unknown, declared read/write hazards and a declared-versus-observed receipt, not on reporting unknown alone; a later opt-in guard (SPEC-058) compiled from declared ownership to host permissions, a companion plugin or an exported snippet; a sketch only for the later layer (SPEC-059): Mailbox plus Whisper by default, Megaphone and Doorbell opt-in and gated by the G1 late-notice harm result and by G2, a separate notification companion, an attributed-write ledger decided after HV-L7, interoperation as documentation only; Agent Braid never launches, messages-as, resumes or authorizes sessions
capabilityDelta.alternative: Path leases and claims (mcp_agent_mail, agent-coord, git-kura, CoProgrammer), live conflict prediction (Clash, DriftWatch), declared-footprint schedulers (OpenWeft, Orchestune), combined-tree and merge-queue integration gates (Radar, SVRF, Gas Town Refinery) and native Claude Code controls (worktree isolation, permissions, TaskCreated hooks, agent teams, cross-session messaging)
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Preregistered at G1: conflicts caught earlier or prevented relative to baseline A0 (prompt partitioning, worktree flag and the SPEC-052 gate) and relative to the native-controls-only arm, false-block and bypass rate, parallelism retained (serialization rate), unknown rate and operator effort on a small paired design; no speed metric
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: Small paired runs of two to four derived tracks on the founder's existing Claude subscription at EUR 0 additional spend, downgraded to observational if a paired design is infeasible

hypothesis.statement: Declared-ownership pre-flight verdicts and declared-versus-observed envelope receipts, with unknown preserved and coverage stated, let an orchestrator catch or avoid some integration problems earlier than baseline A0 without removing parallelism. This is a differentiation hypothesis, untested. The 2026-10-24 prior-art pass found a crowded field of file-level and symbol-level tools, so the possible increment is limited to effect-level hazards, coverage-stated receipts and measured control.
hypothesis.invalidationResult: G1 shows no incremental caught-conflicts or earlier detection over baseline A0, or the observed envelope is mostly unknown, or host verification shows hooks and permissions do not apply inside the target surfaces; the track then closes as watch, rejected or research-only and SPEC-058 is not released.

evidencePlan: Preregister experiment G1 (design, baseline, metrics, kill criterion) before any run
Repeat the dated prior-art pass with the recorded query set before any wording implying uniqueness, before SPEC-058 release and at M4.6 closure
Verify on a host which of the four surfaces honor permissions.deny, sandbox allowlists and plugin hooks inside subagents, teammates and dispatched sessions
Read TeamBus and Orchestune in detail (README beyond the recorded summaries, and a reproduction on a synthetic corpus if feasible) before any read-effect comparison
Reproduce Clash, Radar and one lease tool on a synthetic corpus before any comparative statement; report negative and inconclusive results separately
Keep obtainedEvidence empty until a result is recorded
risks: The field moves quickly: several relevant entrants (Radar, DriftWatch, OpenWeft, Orchestune, TeamBus, SVRF) were not in the 2026-10-23 radar
Most competitor behavior was read from README text and not reproduced
The platform vendor may add native ownership declaration or conflict detection, removing the gap
Reporting missing evidence is not unique (Radar by Jake-Network does it), so the differentiation rests only on the combination, which is untested and could be copied
Host behavior for hooks, permissions and sandbox inside subagents, teammates and dispatched sessions is unverified

G1 compares against baseline A0 only; a native-controls-only comparator such as host permissions or sandbox settings alone is not an arm, so any statement against it needs a separate preregistered design
Enabling any hook component amends ADR 0024 and enforcement is not a grant of authority (ADR 0021); a ledger needs its own ADR and contract G2
Demand for this evidence is not established; the stale-read dogfood datum is a single case with no outcome measured
limits: No evidence obtained; human review pending
Not adoption, host compatibility, superiority or uniqueness; a stage record only
Moving beyond this stage requires the Spec Kit features, ADRs, gate G1 and a founder decision per the adoption pathline
